views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current posture and work the resumed talks to a deal rather than escalate or unilaterally roll back. The Osaka truce gives us the right window — keep the existing 25% tariffs as leverage while pressing China to deliver on its promised farm purchases and structural IP/tech issues, and avoid a new escalation that would break the truce, hammer already-strained farmers, and rattle markets.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is moderate, not existential. We hold the stronger hand: China returned to the table at G20 Osaka and agreed to resume talks with no new tariffs 'for the time being' and to buy unspecified US farm goods, while we merely offered to study easing Huawei restrictions that remain on the entity list (timeline 2019-06-29; Reuters/CNN). That is a favorable terrain — the +0.5 'material GDP drag' anchor is softened by the fact that the US extracted a truce without giving up the tariff hammer. However, the costs are real and justify not celebrating: the 10-year yield fell from 2.74% to 2.06% and the 2-year from 2.58% to 1.83% (country_health DGS10/DGS2), a sharp flattening that signals growth drag and Fed-easing expectations from the dispute; industrial production has slipped (INDPRO 102.8 to 101.9); and the farm belt is the acute exposure — US soybean exports to China plunged ~74% by volume, net farm income has fallen ~50% since 2013, and farm groups are pressing hard for a settlement (ASA May 13, 2019; farmpolicy reports July 2019). That domestic political pressure and market signal keeps the threat off the opportunity end of the scale, but the truce and resumed talks keep it well short of high threat. On action: escalating now would shatter the truce, deepen farm-belt losses and spook markets; full concession would forfeit our leverage before China has matched with a comprehensive offer. The correct stance is negotiate — hold tariffs as bargaining capital and convert the resumption of talks into a real settlement, consistent with the +0.1 action score and the 'negotiate' action level.
key_factors: G20 Osaka truce June 29: talks resumed, no new tariffs, Huawei easing under study but entity list intact
Tariff leverage intact: 25% on ~$200B plus list of remaining imports
Yield curve flattening (10y 2.74→2.06, 2y 2.58→1.83) signals growth drag and market concern
Farm-belt exposure: US soybean exports to China down ~74%, net farm income -50%, growers demanding a deal
Reuters/CNN/WaPo: talks 'back on track,' China agreed to farm purchases but structural issues unresolved

sources_cited.excerpt: G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs 'for the time being.' Trump says he will ease some Huawei restrictions (Huawei remains on the Entity List).
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List.
Soybean prices 20-25% below pre-tariff levels; US soybean exports to China plunged 74% by volume; farm income down 50%.
US-China agree to restart trade talks; no new tariffs; China to buy US farm products; tariffs remain in place while negotiations resume.
